papers.title: Acyclicity and simultaneous protection of individual core maxima
papers.exact_claim: For a fixed connected allowed interaction graph G on K>=2 equal-sized sectors, the worst leximin ideal fraction c(G) and the worst best-achievable simultaneous fraction R(G) both equal 1/K for trees and 0 for cyclic G. The triangle family has exact best simultaneous fraction 1/(2q+3).
limits: Nonnegative real pair matrices, productive full teams only, integral matching worth, positive grand worth and a nonempty entire core are essential. Zero pair matrices are allowed.
Cyclic zero is an infimum over growing finite markets; every finite admissible market still has positive best simultaneous protection.
Does not cover arbitrary productive partial teams; integral matching does not mean integer-valued input weights.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotic separation of opposing egalitarian core selections
papers.exact_claim: For singleton-normalized exact TU games with n players and positive total T, s_n=sup ||Lmin-Lmax||_1/T satisfies 2-s_n=2/n+O(log(n)/n^2), hence n(2-s_n)->2. Lmax minimizes descending sorted payoffs. A universal compact-convex overlap inequality and whole-core Fibonacci segments establish the asymptotic comparison.
limits: Not an exact finite-n formula, a unique-extremizer classification or an aggregate welfare-loss claim. Half the normalized L1 distance is the fraction of surplus changing recipients.
The construction must identify the entire core; an arbitrary feasible segment inside the core is insufficient.

papers.title: Fair core selections: a sharp boundary between pairs and triples
papers.exact_claim: For unit-capacity nonnegative graph matching games with positive total T and nonempty entire core, the sharp normalized distance rho=||Lmin-Lmax||_1/T is floor(n/2)/(floor(n/2)+1) for n>=4 (and zero for n=2,3). Sparse strict triple markets with bounded values in {0,1,2,3} approach rho=2. Complete equal-sided additive triples have a one-third ideal guarantee and sharp distance supremum 4/3.
limits: All players, including isolates and padded dummies, count toward n.
The triple result is a supremum over growing populations, not a fixed-size classification. These matching games need not be exact TU games.
Arbitrary triple arrays, the complete additive benchmark and P1's pair-additive graph technology are different domains.

papers.title: Balanced transport at the egalitarian core: a complete boundary phase diagram
papers.exact_claim: At a strict Lmin payoff boundary in a singleton-normalized exact game, let m be the number of poorer players and h the number of richer players. Slack of the richer suffix is possible iff m>=m_min(h), where m_min(1)=4, m_min(2)=m_min(3)=3, and m_min(h)=2 for h>=4. Necessity uses tight-coalition geometry and balanced transport; explicit realizing families prove sufficiency.
limits: Poorer players need not share a payoff.
The main dimension-free theorem has stronger review coverage than auxiliary finite selection/certificate claims. Restricted split censuses are not universal uniqueness results.

papers.title: Core stability does not imply egalitarian stability: a sharp six-player counterexample
papers.exact_claim: The exact, monotone, superadditive game v(S)=min{A(S),B(S)} with A=(1,1,0,1,3,0) and B=(2,0,1,0,1,2) has entire core [A,B], which is von Neumann-Morgenstern stable, while the procedural egalitarian solution lies outside it. Terminal claims total 13/2 although T=6. The final efficient allocation is (3/2,1/2,1,1/2,3/2,1), paying coalition {5,6} only 5/2 against worth 3. The package gives a direct stability proof and complete three-regime additive ray.
limits: This example is not singleton-normalized. Terminal claims are not the final efficient allocation.
Six-player minimality uses established low-player implications.
The procedural egalitarian rule differs from P2/P3's opposing sorted selectors.

papers.title: Sharp subsidies for protecting core maxima in three-sided assignment markets
papers.exact_claim: Freeze H_i at each owner's individual maximum over the original entire efficient core, and minimize s(v)=sum_i y_i-T subject to all coalition constraints and y_i>=H_i/3. In strict equal-sized three-sector nonnegative pair-additive full-team markets with positive T and nonempty original core, s(v)<T/3 for every finite admissible market, while sup_v s(v)/T=1/3. The separate integral obstruction bound 2(k-1)T/[3(2k-1)] is sharp for k>=2.
limits: Static fixed-game result; no reporting-incentive guarantee.
Individual maxima need not be simultaneously attainable. Total funding has supremum 4/3, whereas one third refers to the external subsidy.
The integral refinement is not the full fractional optimum at every fixed market size. General-sector sharpness and unrestricted rational short-flow bounds remain open.

papers.title: Sharp subsidies for truthful production and network cooperation
papers.exact_claim: For f(c)=min_k w^k.c with at most K fixed nonnegative forms, the optimal worst-case all-profile total-payment factor under individual own-bundle monotonicity and all-coalition coverage is B_K=(1+o(1)) log(K)/log(log(K)). A capped hybrid proves the upper, and weighted report transitions give a matching leading-constant lower on simple DAGs with strategic auxiliary owners. For finite-valued monotone concave homogeneous production, including support-boundary discontinuities, the current general factor is min{d,n*sqrt(2/(n+1)),1+2*sqrt(d)}.
limits: Incentives concern binding coordinatewise underreports and payment-only individual utility, not collusion, outside production, private costs, overreports or identity splitting.
K can be exponential in a compact network description; polynomial-time evaluation or certification is not guaranteed.

Restricted fixed-mask/common-support square-root barriers do not settle unrestricted owner/dimension rates. Choosing among general upper rules uses fixed public parameters before reports, not a pointwise minimum of payment vectors.

papers.title: The cost of coalition withholding: resource dimension and coalition size
papers.exact_claim: Sharp universal coalition factors D_d=(d+1)/2 and D_d^OUT=1+c(d-1), where c*(2-exp(-1/c))=1. For sparse packing, K_r(s)<=K_r^OUT(s)<=r*s^(r-1); arbitrary-rule arity-three lower K_3(s)>=sqrt(s/6), with sharper B_s asymptotic to sqrt(2*pi*s)/(3*sqrt(e)) and B_6=493/243. Fixed arity r>=3 has lower Omega_r(s^((r-2)/(r-1))). The graph section gives full-OUT factor 1+1/sqrt(2) on unit-profit P4, complete blow-ups and disjoint unions; a separate P6 example blocks the defined fixed-leaf-reserve layerwise recursion.
